nodes.name: DIVIDE() Function
nodes.summary: DAX function that performs safe division, returning BLANK() when the denominator is 0 or BLANK instead of throwing an arithmetic overflow error.

nodes.name: VAR/RETURN Pattern
nodes.summary: DAX pattern using named variables before RETURN to make multi-step calculations readable, debuggable, and maintainable. Each intermediate result is named and calculated once.

nodes.name: Use DIVIDE Instead of / Operator
nodes.summary: When dividing in DAX, always use DIVIDE(a, b, alt) instead of the / operator. DIVIDE handles zero and BLANK denominators gracefully by returning BLANK(), avoiding arithmetic overflow errors.

nodes.name: DAX User-Defined Function (UDF)
nodes.summary: A typed, named, documented DAX function defined once in a semantic model that can be called from any measure expression. Provides a stable interface hiding internal complexity.

nodes.name: Calculation Group
nodes.summary: A Tabular feature that lets users toggle between alternative definitions of the same KPI via a slicer. Contains calculation items (e.g., Actual, Budget, Forecast) that modify measure behavior when selected.

nodes.name: Format String Expression
nodes.summary: A property on a calculation item that controls how the converted or modified value is displayed, allowing currency-specific or measure-specific format strings.

nodes.name: SELECTEDMEASUREFORMATSTRING()
nodes.summary: A DAX function that returns the format string of the currently executing measure, used inside Format String Expressions to detect whether to apply currency formatting or preserve the measure's original format.

nodes.name: SELECTEDMEASURENAME()
nodes.summary: A DAX function that returns the name of the currently executing measure as a string, enabling conditional logic in Format String Expressions to distinguish between monetary and ratio measures.

nodes.name: UDFs Enable Safe AI Copilot Adoption
nodes.summary: Typed documented UDFs serve as a black-box contract with a named interface, parameter types, and IntelliSense descriptions. This allows AI copilots and junior developers to call measures correctly without reverse-engineering nested CALCULATE logic.

nodes.name: UDFs Require Compatibility Level 1702+
nodes.summary: DAX UDFs are only available on semantic models with compatibility level 1702 or higher. On older models, the FUNCTION block fails silently with no obvious error message, and the function does not appear in Model Explorer after deployment.

nodes.name: UDFs and Calculation Groups Solve Different Problems
nodes.summary: UDFs define how logic is computed (the how) with explicit typed parameters at the call site, while calculation groups control which measure is selected (the which) via slicer selection. They are complementary and compose together in mature semantic models.

nodes.name: DAX UDF Development Environments
nodes.summary: Five entry points for building, testing, and deploying DAX UDFs: DAX Query View (interactive testing), TMDL View (Git version control), Model Explorer (ad-hoc creation), XMLA/SSMS (CI/CD DevOps), and Semantic Link Labs (Fabric notebook automation).

nodes.name: Like-for-Like Comparison Pattern
nodes.summary: A DAX pattern that filters a measure to only include entities (stores, products, customers) that were active throughout the entire selected time period, enabling valid year-over-year comparisons by excluding entities that opened or closed mid-period.

nodes.name: TREATAS() Function
nodes.summary: A DAX function that creates virtual relationships by treating the results of a table expression as filter values for a specified column, used to apply entity-status filters in like-for-like patterns.

nodes.name: KEEPFILTERS() Function
nodes.summary: A DAX function that applies filter arguments without removing existing filters, preserving context when wrapping CALCULATE filter arguments in patterns like like-for-like comparisons.

nodes.name: Dynamic Graph Area Buffer Pattern
nodes.summary: A visualization pattern that adds a 5% padding above the maximum and 5% below the minimum vital values when setting the Y-axis range, creating a buffer zone so data lines do not sit flush against chart edges.

nodes.name: MAXX/MINX ALL Date Dynamic Range
nodes.summary: DAX pattern using MAXX and MINX with ALL() on a date column to compute the full-date-range maximum and minimum values for a measure, used as the basis for dynamic Y-axis range calculations.

nodes.name: Evergreen Top-N Products Identified by Coverage Threshold
nodes.summary: A product qualifies as evergreen (stable top performer) when it appears in the top-N list in at least a configurable coverage percentage of all reporting periods (e.g., 80% of years). Uses GENERATE, GROUPBY, and FILTER over ALLSELECTED() periods.

nodes.name: DAX Is Context-Driven vs Excel Cell-Based
nodes.summary: Excel uses cell-position references (A1, B2) and manual propagation chains that break at scale. DAX uses table/column references with filter and row context that automatically propagate across all visuals and scale to millions of rows in a semantic model.

nodes.name: DAX Measure Best Practices
nodes.summary: Guidelines for writing maintainable DAX measures: always write explicit measures (never drag columns), use DIVIDE instead of /, name base measures clearly, layer logic through composition, use VAR/RETURN for readability, never self-reference measures, and use CALCULATE for context transition inside iterators.

nodes.name: Use CALCULATE for Context Transition Inside Iterators
nodes.summary: When iterating with SUMX, AVERAGEX, etc., use CALCULATE([measure]) inside the iterator so each row gets its own filtered measure value rather than the outer context's aggregated value.

nodes.name: DaxPatterns.LikeForLike UDF Library
nodes.summary: A three-function model-independent library from SQLBI for like-for-like comparisons: EntityStatus creates an Active/Inactive status table per period, ComputeForSameEntity filters a measure to only active entities, and StoreSalesForSameStore applies the pattern to sales.

nodes.name: Currency Conversion Format String Pattern
nodes.summary: DAX pattern for a Currency Conversion calculation item Format String Expression that conditionally applies currency-specific format strings from a Currency table while preserving the original format for non-monetary ratio and count measures.

nodes.name: SELECTEDVALUE() Function
nodes.summary: A DAX function that returns the value of a column if there is exactly one value in the current filter context, or a specified default if there are zero or multiple values. Used in Format String Expressions as a fallback when a calculation group column is not in the visual.

nodes.name: SkipConversion Logic in Format String Expressions
nodes.summary: In a Currency Conversion Format String Expression, detecting whether a measure name contains '#' or '%' (indicating a ratio or count measure) allows the expression to skip currency formatting and preserve the original measure format, preventing incorrect formatting on non-monetary KPIs.

Evergreen Top-N and the currency format string pattern both use measure name detection but for opposite purposes: Evergreen identifies products by matching in period lists while the format string pattern identifies measure types by detecting '#' or '%' in the name.

The currency conversion pattern uses SELECTEDMEASUREFORMATSTRING() to retrieve and preserve the original measure format for non-currency measures.
The currency conversion pattern uses SELECTEDMEASURENAME() to detect whether the active measure is a monetary measure requiring currency formatting.
The currency conversion pattern uses SELECTEDVALUE() with SELECTEDMEASURENAME() as fallback to get the current measure name from either the Metric calculation group or the report measure.
